The present Appeal has been filed on behalf of the Appellant under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 impugning the judgment dated 09.06.2025 [hereinafter referred to as "Impugned Award"] passed by the learned Presiding Officer, MACT, Shahdara, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi in MACT No. 761/2018 titled Poonam & Ors. v. Nooruddin & Ors.

By the Impugned Order,
compensation in the sum of Rs. 26,48,288/- has been awarded along with interest at the rate of 7%
per annum.
2. Learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the Appellant submits that the challenge in the present Appeal is on two grounds.
First, on the issue of contributory negligence.

He submits that the Claim Petition i.e. MACT No. 761/2018 was listed with another case being MACT no. 702/2018 captioned Savita Verma & Ors. v. Nooruddin & Ors. and that the evidence in the present case as well as in the connected case was led together in view of the fact that it was the same accident.

sentences.text: 4. Learned Counsel appearing for the Appellant submits that the Respondent No. 1/injured was admittedly a part time school teacher, however, her salary as a school teacher has been taken into consideration for calculation of loss of future income and not the income earned from her tuitions.

5. The examination of the Impugned Award shows that the Respondent No. 1/injured has admitted to being a part time school teacher, however, the learned Tribunal gave a finding that even after the accident, the Respondent No. 1/injured meets her part financial responsibilities by taking tuitions.

It was further held that by the learned Tribunal that the Respondent No. 1/injured is still able to earn income from the tuition but she is not able to continue the job as teacher because of the long standing hours.

Thus, the learned Tribunal has assessed the loss of future income as Rs. 26,250/-
per month based on her previous salary.
6. It is apposite to set out paragraph 36 of the Impugned Award in this behalf.
This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 10/07/2025 at 21:39:16 "36.
As discussed above, the income of petitioner has been assessed to be Rs.26,250/- per month.

Further, the petitioner (PWl) has fairly admitted in her cross-examination conducted by learned counsel for respondent no.l and 2 that, after the accident, she meets her part financial responsibilities by taking tuition from which, on an average, she receives Rs. 10,000 to Rs. 12,000/-
per month.
PWl stated that she takes tuition in English and other subjects and she receives the tuition fees in cash and on some occasions through online mode.

In view of her said admission, it is apparent that she is still able to earn the income from tuition, which she had been taking prior to the accident also as per her .affidavit of examination-in-chief but she is not able to continue her job as Teacher in school because of long-standing hours there.

Therefore, for the purpose of assessing the loss of future income, her income from salary as school teacher i.e. Rs.26,250/- only has to be taken into consideration."
7.
Issue Notice.
7.1 On steps being taken, let Notice be served on the Respondents via all modes.
Affidavit of service be filed within two weeks.
8. Subject to the deposit of entire decretal amount inclusive of up-to-date interest within a period of 6 weeks, the operation of the Impugned Award shall remain stayed till the next date of hearing.
In the event, there is any default in depositing the amount, the interim protection granted by this Court shall automatically stand vacated.

9. Upon deposit by the Appellant, 60% of the deposited amount inclusive of up to date interest shall be released to the Respondent No. 1/injured in accordance with scheme, as is set out in the Impugned Award.
